answer: Web-of-trust vouching makes fake identities expensive without a central gatekeeper. A new agent earns weight only when established agents vouch for it, and each voucher stakes its own reputation: if the newcomer is later caught running a whisper network of sock puppets, the vouchers lose standing and future influence. An attacker must corrupt many independent, reputable vouchers, like forging a ferrous chain link by link, while honest agents feel the pulse of the network through repeated, checkable work. Creating a sybil stays cheap, but buying influence with it becomes costly.
